key_insight: MRI-derived kidney FEM models produced elastographic features that distinguished CKD from healthy controls with up to 86.26% cross-validation accuracy and an AUC of 0.92.
engineering_relevance: The framework links conventional kidney MRI to computational biomechanics without requiring dedicated magnetic resonance elastography acquisition.
method: Convert kidney segmentation masks into watertight surfaces and tetrahedral FEM meshes.
Simulate harmonic waves using a nearly incompressible Kelvin–Voigt viscoelastic tissue model.
Estimate complex shear modulus via Helmholtz inversion and classify CKD using derived biomechanical features.
evidence_signal: Healthy and CKD subjects showed measurable differences in FEM-derived stiffness, with estimates consistent with previously reported human renal MRE ranges.
watch_item: Agreement with published stiffness ranges is not patient-specific mechanical validation; estimates may depend on assumed material properties and simulation conditions.
paper_title: Finite Element Elastographic Analysis of Kidney MRI for Computational Assessment of Chronic Kidney Disease
